name: Great Britain – no capacity component (half-hourly settlement)
assumed: That a domestic supply in Great Britain has no measured capacity component. The source is HLD §8's 2026-09-19 market survey — energy on N2EX half-hourly, Agile and DFS events, grid time-of-use "none / Day-Night-Peak", peak component `NoPeak`, hard limit the fuse — and not a published charging statement, because there is no figure to publish: a domestic tariff is a standing charge per day plus a unit rate per kWh, and the DNO's capacity costs sit inside the unit rate rather than being measured against the household's own peak. What would replace this note is a reference into the site DNO's use-of-system charging statement showing a domestic band with no capacity charge. If a supplier ever offers a domestic capacity charge it arrives here as a new version with its own `valid_from` (INV-52). Demand Flexibility Service rewards are price-axis events for D1, not a capacity metric, and are deliberately absent.
